experiment: REAL offloaded-KV decode microbenchmark (CPU pinned KV, PCIe fetch, CUDA-stream a-layer-ahead prefetch, real attention matmuls @ Llama-3.1-8B shapes)
honest_findings: MATCHED-QUALITY (prefetch_hot vs reactive_hot, both attend hot h=0.25): real TPOT -21%/-18%/-16% at 16/32/64K. The clean latency-hiding win. NOTE: smaller than my earlier analytical model (-35..-42%) -- the model overestimated stream-overlap; real sync + on-demand miss fetch eat in.
vs FlexGen fetch-all (full quality): -66%/-70%/-72% -- but hot-vs-full quality tradeoff (needs Pareto).
Real overlap works: prefetch_hot < reactive_hot at every ctx, confirming the a-layer-ahead query-free prefetch hides fetch latency.
caveats: Faithful TPOT microbenchmark: real DMA + real attention/MLP matmuls @ real shapes + real CUDA streams, random weights (timing is shape-driven, not values). Not the full model's fused kernels (those would be faster compute -> MORE IO-bound -> prefetch helps MORE, so this is conservative).
Quality axis comes from the separate real-model LongBench F1 (hot fraction == budget).
